#9656. Sellfy Review 2022: How Good Is This Ecommerce Platform?

Are you searching for an ecomerce platform to help you build an online store and sell products?

In this Sellfy review, we'll talk about how this eCommerce platform can let you sell digital products while keeping full control of your marketing.

And the best part? Starting your business can be done in just five minutes.

Let us then talk about the Sellfy platform and all the benefits it can bring to your business.

Sellfy is an eCommerce solution that allows digital content creators, including writers, illustrators, designers, musicians, and filmmakers, to sell their products online. Sellfy provides a customizable storefront where users can display their digital products and embed "Buy Now" buttons on their website or blog. Sellfy product pages enable users to showcase their products from different angles with multiple images and previews from Soundcloud, Vimeo, and YouTube. Files of up to 2GB can be uploaded to Sellfy, and the company offers unlimited bandwidth and secure file storage. Users can also embed their entire store or individual project widgets in their site, with the ability to preview how widgets will appear before they are displayed.

Sellfy is a powerful e-commerce platform that helps you personalize your online storefront. You can add your logo, change colors, revise navigation, and edit the layout of your store. Sellfy also allows you to create a full shopping cart so customers can purchase multiple items. And Sellfy gives you the ability to set your language or let customers see a translated version of your store based on their location.

Sellfy gives you the option to host your store directly on its platform, add a custom domain to your store, and use it as an embedded storefront on your website. Sellfy also optimizes its store offerings for mobile devices, allowing for a seamless checkout experience.

Sellfy allows creators to host all their products and sell all of their digital products on one platform. Sellfy also does not place storage limits on your store but recommends that files be no larger than 5GB. Creators can sell both standard and subscription-based products in any file format that is supported by the online marketplace. Customers can purchase products instantly after making a purchase – there is no waiting period.

You can organize your store by creating your product categories, sorting by any characteristic you choose. Your title, description, and the image will be included on each product page. In this way, customers can immediately evaluate all of your products. You can offer different pricing options for all of your products, including "pay what you want," in which the price is entirely up to the customer. This option allows you to give customers control over the cost of individual items (without a minimum price) or to set pricing minimums—a good option if you're in a competitive market or when you have higher-end products. You can also offer set prices per product as well as free products to help build your store's popularity.

Sellfy is ideal for selling digital content, such as ebooks. But it does not allow you to copyrighted material (that you don't have rights to distribute).

Sellfy offers several ways to share your store, enabling you to promote your business on different platforms. Sellfy lets you integrate it with your existing website using "buy now" buttons, embed your entire storefront, or embed certain products so you can reach more people. Sellfy also enables you to connect with your Facebook page and YouTube channel, maximizing your visibility.

Sellfy is a simple online platform that allows customers to buy your products directly through your store. Sellfy has two payment processing options: PayPal and Stripe. You will receive instant payments with both of these processors, and your customer data is protected by Sellfy's secure (PCI-compliant) payment security measures. In addition to payment security, Sellfy provides anti-fraud tools to help protect your products including PDF stamping, unique download links, and limited download attempts.

To expand functionality and make your e-commerce store run more efficiently, Sellfy offers several integrations. Google Analytics and Webhooks, as well as integrations with Patreon and Facebook Live Chat, are just a few of the options available. Sellfy allows you to connect to Zapier, which gives you access to hundreds of third-party apps, including tools like Mailchimp, Trello, Salesforce, and more.

Sellfy has its benefits and downsides, but fortunately, the pros outweigh the cons.

#9655. Taking Trainium3 to the Track: Generating Videos with LTX-2.5

Thanks to our partnership with AWS, we were lucky enough to get access to a Trainium3 machine (trn3.48xlarge, 64 NeuronCores) for a month. We spent most of the month testing Hugging Face models on it, and getting more of them to work.

With five days left, I allowed myself a little fun. When you have a Ferrari, every now and then you want to take it out on the track. So I asked myself: what if I tried to generate videos?

I picked LTX-2.5 from Lightricks, which generates video and sound together. By the end, once the models were loaded, a 10-second clip with sound took 22 to 23 s to generate, on half of the machine. Here is the result.

I had two goals. The first was to see how easy it is to generate videos with diffusers on Trainium3. Not the simple clips from the examples: I wanted to make short films from a script, closer to a real use case, like drafting a movie. The second was performance. I wanted to get close to what you get with CUDA, or with LTX's own API.

For CUDA, I found no real figure to compare against. The only one is LTX's claim of 6.8 s for a 10-second 720p clip on four B200 GPUs, with no detail on how it was measured. So I set CUDA aside and compared with LTX's online API instead, which LTX says makes a 10-second 1080p clip in 23.7 s. In the end, the setup matches it, and even beats it by about a second: 22 to 23 s for a 10-second clip at 2048×1024, once the models are loaded, on half of the machine. Not bad, considering how little time I had to optimize the pipelines.

The input is a film: a JSON list of shots, each with a name and a prompt, much like a storyboard. LTX-2.5 does better with long prompts, so each prompt is a paragraph on the style, the subject, the motion, the camera, the light and the sound. Here is the seal film's file, with the prompts shortened:

Each shot has a name and a prompt, and can have a seed, to keep the take I picked among several. Shots are chained with two keys. This chaining is the point, since prompts alone do not keep a subject from one shot to the next:

A shot can also be trimmed, or have a caption drawn over it.

Making a film from shots works like animation, which has two ways to go. Straight ahead, each shot continues the one before. Pose to pose, you make the key shot first, until you get one you like; then the shots before it end on its first frames (to), and the shots after it start from its last frames (from). When a film builds up to a payoff (the moment everything was leading to), the payoff is the key shot. I found this order by trial and error, and made the seal film pose to pose, starting from iceberg.

The payoff is iceberg: the iceberg rolls over, and its wave drenches the seal. nap, the sleeping seal, ends on the first 9 frames of iceberg (to), so that the seal, the floe and the iceberg stay the same into the payoff. shake starts from the last 25 frames of iceberg (from): the dripping seal shakes off the water and flops down on the floe. The dream is made on its own, and a cut joins it to the rest.

On the diffusers side, three pipelines share the models of LTX-2.5. LTX2Pipeline makes the shots from their prompt alone, and LTX2ConditionPipeline makes the shots that start or end on frames of another shot. These two follow the two-stage distilled recipe of the model card: 8 steps, then the third pipeline, LTX2LatentUpsamplePipeline, upscales the latents ×2 before 3 final steps.

The diffusers pipelines do all of the generation. The film part is about 160 lines of Python on top: read the film file, order the shots so each keyframe exists before the shot that needs it, and cut the frames to hand over; then trim, caption, even out the sound and assemble the film. The code is in dacorvo/video-generation. The films I kept are in the dacorvo/video-generation bucket, with their JSON files: the seal, the fox, and the goat, which trims two of its shots and draws a caption over its payoff.

Out of the box, the model does not run on the NeuronCores: the transformer does not fit on one, and diffusers has no plan to split it. The first attempt that ran (the model card's pipeline, with the transformer split over 4 cores and a few patches) took about 5 min 20 s for a 10-second clip, and the NeuronCores were actually computing for only about 45 s of it. What's more, the target resolution was out of reach.

Getting there took three kinds of work: making the model run on the NeuronCores (requires tensor parallelism), splitting it over more of them (sequence parallelism), and making the host keep up with them.

Most of the fixes below are on the device, and that is where most of the effort went. The biggest end-to-end savings came from the host: the low-hanging fruit, since that is obviously where the waste was.

Three issues were never explained: the transformer compiled as one graph returned NaN at one size, the first shot that ends on keyframes was slow in each new process (even with every graph in the cache), and the latent upsampler fails to load next to the transformer, so it stays on the CPU.

Some of this is being fixed upstream. diffusers#15420 (open) fixes the LTX-2 pipelines, which would make the second workaround above unnecessary. diffusers#14725 (still open) brings tensor and context parallelism into one ParallelConfig, and a _tp_plan for LTX-2.5 is planned.

On the performance side, once the models are loaded, a 10-second 2048×1024 clip with sound takes 22 to 23 s. That rivals LTX's paid API, on half of the instance. A service would keep its processes up, as they take about 3 minutes to load the models, and 80 s for their first clip.

On the feature side, diffusers has what it takes to draft a movie. The shots come from prompts, and keep their subject from one shot to the next by starting or ending on frames of other shots. Takes differ by their seed, and the film file keeps the one I picked. Re-run with the same code and film file, and you get the same film back, byte for byte. A shot can also start from an image, such as a storyboard frame or a character sheet, which the condition pipeline takes the same way as frames (I did not try it in a film).

LTX calls LTX-2.5 a world model, with robotics as an emerging use. Robots, cars and drones learn from videos of what their cameras see, and a world model can make more of them, including events too rare or too risky to film. So I also tried it on real footage, with the same code: a shot can start from the first second of a real camera clip and invent what happens next. One frame was not enough, as the model cannot tell from it how fast things move.

Here is the head camera of a Fourier GR1-T2 humanoid robot (a clip from NVIDIA's GR1-100), looking down at a table. In the real 6-second clip, the robot's left hand picks an orange from a plate and drops it in a tray. The model only sees the first second of that clip (the hands raised, before anything moves) and invents the rest. What really happened, next to its invention:

Same scene, same pick: the model invents the grab on its own, and keeps the table, the hands and the fruit consistent with the real footage. More interesting are the events that did not happen. From the same second, with only the prompt changed, a person leans over and grabs the orange too, and the human hand and the robot hand carry it to the tray together. Five takes, with the real footage first:

The person's gestures and timing differ in each take, and the robot's arm adapts to them. That is the appeal for training: not one continuation of a clip, but a distribution of them, each reproducible from its film file and seed.

The robotics folder of the bucket has the five takes with their JSON files, and a second example from the front camera of a car in a snowstorm (Boreas), where the alternate event is slush thrown on the lens by a passing truck. Asked to make the car accelerate instead, the model kept its speed: the prompt does not override what the first second of footage already implies.

These videos follow prompts, not the robot's or car's commands: a training setup would need generation conditioned on those actions. For that, a team fine-tunes the pre-trained checkpoint of LTX-2.5 on the frames and actions of its own robots.

The Ferrari made it around the track, on half of its cylinders.

#9654. Handling Disconnects, Token Leaks, and Tool Calls in Vercel AI SDK 4

The "hello world" of the Vercel AI SDK looks deceptively simple: import streamText, pass a prompt, return toDataStreamResponse(), and render on the client with useChat. In a clean localhost sandbox, it feels like magic.

Then you ship to production, and reality hits.

Users close their browser tabs midway through a 2,000-token completion, leaving your serverless function quietly paying OpenAI for tokens nobody will ever read. Or your model decides to hallucinate an extra nested field during a multi-step tool call, triggering an unhandled Zod validation error that crashes the Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream without an error payload. If you are rendering Generative UI artifacts, mismatched server and client states cause React hydration blowups.

Let’s address three essential production patterns to bulletproof your Vercel AI SDK 4.x streaming workflows.

When a user closes their tab or clicks "Stop generating," the client drops the TCP connection. However, unless you explicitly bind the incoming request's abort signal to the model call, your server route continues consuming tokens upstream.

Here is how to wire an AbortSignal properly in a Next.js App Router route:

If the client drops the SSE socket, req.signal aborts immediately, halting the upstream model invocation and saving your API budget.

When using autonomous tool calling with maxSteps, LLMs frequently hallucinate stringified booleans, missing optional fields, or loose array syntax. If your Zod schema is too rigid, the SDK throws a validation error and aborts the entire conversation loop.

Use Zod coercion and preprocessors to ensure resilient parsing:

By coercing numbers and preprocessing loose arrays, your tool survives edge-case model generations without throwing unhandled schema exceptions.

When chaining autonomous tools, models can enter infinite loops if a tool returns empty or ambiguous data. Always define explicit bounds using maxSteps and an empty-check fallback:

Setting maxSteps strictly confines the agent loop while still giving the model enough freedom to search, evaluate, and formulate a synthesized final response.

If you want to skip debugging Edge runtime stream aborts, hydration mismatches in Generative UI, and brittle tool schemas from scratch, check out The Vercel AI SDK & Generative UI Vault.

#9652. Migrating WooCommerce customers and orders to Shopify: what transfers, what does not, and a Python CSV converter

Moving a store from WooCommerce to Shopify sounds like one job. In practice it's three: products, customers and orders, and each one moves differently. Products are the easy part. Customers come across with some gaps you need to plan for. Orders are where most people get stuck, because the tool they used for the first two doesn't handle them.

This post covers what transfers, what doesn't, and a short Python script that turns a WooCommerce customer export into a file Shopify's customer import accepts.

Transfers cleanly: names, email addresses, a default address, phone numbers (if they're in a format Shopify accepts), company names, and anything you choose to carry over as tags or notes.

Doesn't transfer: passwords. WordPress stores password hashes, not passwords, and Shopify can't use those hashes. Every imported customer has to set up access again. With Shopify's classic customer accounts you send account invites so they can set a new password. With the newer customer accounts there are no passwords at all; customers sign in with a one-time code sent to their email, so the "reset your password" problem goes away. Either way, tell customers before launch so the change doesn't look like a security problem.

Needs a different tool: historical orders. The CSV import in the Shopify admin covers products and customers. It doesn't import past orders. For those you need an app, such as Shopify's Store Migration app or Matrixify, or a script against the Shopify Admin API. Keep the old WooCommerce order number somewhere on each imported order (in the order name, a tag or a note) so your support team can find an order when a customer quotes the old number.

Depends on third parties: subscriptions and saved cards. Saved payment tokens belong to your payment gateway, not to WooCommerce, and recurring billing belongs to your subscription plugin. Whether active subscriptions can carry on without customers re-entering card details depends on the gateway and the Shopify subscription app you pick. Ask both before you set a launch date.

WooCommerce stores billing details as user meta with keys like billing_first_name, billing_city and billing_country. Most export plugins can output these as columns. This sample uses those names plus a marketing_opt_in column from a newsletter plugin. Adjust the names in the script to match your own export.

Row 104 is a duplicate of 101 with different capitalisation, and row 105 has no email. Both are common in real exports.

Standard library only. It writes Shopify's customer import columns, lowercases and de-duplicates emails, and tags every row woo-import.

Customer and order data is the part of a migration you can't redo cheaply after launch, so it's worth a dry run. If you'd like help planning or running the move, Dzimark's Shopify migration team builds Shopify stores and migrations for businesses in the USA, UK, Canada and Australia.

Can I move customer passwords from WooCommerce to Shopify? No. WordPress only keeps password hashes, and Shopify can't use them. Customers either set a new password from an account invite or, with Shopify's newer customer accounts, sign in with a one-time code by email.

Can I import past orders with the Shopify admin CSV import? No. The admin import handles products and customers. Use a migration app such as Store Migration or Matrixify, or the Admin API, for historical orders.

#9651. ProWritingAid VS Grammarly: Which Grammar Checker is Better in (2022) ?

ProWritingAid VS Grammarly:  When it comes to English grammar, there are two Big Players that everyone knows of: the Grammarly and ProWritingAid. but you are wondering which one to choose so here we write a detail article which will help you to choose the best one for you so Let's start

What is Grammarly?

Grammarly is a tool that checks for grammatical errors, spelling, and punctuation.it gives you comprehensive feedback on your writing. You can use this tool to proofread and edit articles, blog posts, emails, etc.

Grammarly also detects all types of mistakes, including sentence structure issues and misused words. It also gives you suggestions on style changes, punctuation, spelling, and grammar all are in real-time. The free version covers the basics like identifying grammar and spelling mistakes

whereas the Premium version offers a lot more functionality, it detects plagiarism in your content, suggests word choice, or adds fluency to it.


Features of Grammarly

  • Spelling and Word Suggestion: Grammarly detects basic to advance grammatical errors and also help you why this is an error and suggest to you how you can improve it
  • Create a Personal Dictionary: The Grammarly app allows you to add words to your personal dictionary so that the same mistake isn't highlighted every time you run Grammarly.
  • Different English Style: Check to spell for American, British, Canadian, and Australian English.
  • Plagiarism: This feature helps you detect if a text has been plagiarized by comparing it with over eight billion web pages.
  • Wordiness: This tool will help you check your writing for long and hard-to-read sentences. It also shows you how to shorten sentences so that they are more concise.
  • Passive Voice: The program also notifies users when passive voice is used too frequently in a document.
  • Punctuations: This feature flags all incorrect and missing punctuation.
  • Repetition: The tool provides recommendations for replacing the repeated word.
  • Proposition: Grammarly identifies misplaced and confused prepositions.

  • Plugins: It offers Microsoft Word, Microsoft Outlook, and Google Chrome plugins.


What is ProWritingAid?

ProWritingAid is a style and grammar checker for content creators and writers. It helps to optimize word choice, punctuation errors, and common grammar mistakes, providing detailed reports to help you improve your writing. 

ProWritingAid can be used as an add-on to WordPress, Gmail, and Google Docs. The software also offers helpful articles, videos, quizzes, and explanations to help improve your writing.

Features of ProWriting Aid

Here are some key features of ProWriting Aid:

  • Grammar checker and spell checker: This tool helps you to find all grammatical and spelling errors.
  • Find repeated words:  The tool also allows you to search for repeated words and phrases in your content.
  • Context-sensitive style suggestions:  You can find the exact style of writing you intend and suggest if it flows well in your writing.
  • Check the readability of your content: Pro Writing Aid helps you identify the strengths and weaknesses of your article by pointing out difficult sentences and paragraphs.
  • Sentence Length: It also indicates the length of your sentences.
  • Check Grammatical error: It also checks your work for any grammatical errors or typos, as well.
  • Overused words: As a writer, you might find yourself using the same word repeatedly. ProWritingAid's overused words checker helps you avoid this lazy writing mistake.
  • Consistency: Check your work for inconsistent usage of open and closed quotation marks.
  • Echoes: Check your writing for uniformly repetitive words and phrases.

Difference between Grammarly and Pro-Writing Aid

Grammarly and ProWritingAid are well-known grammar-checking software. However, if you're like most people who can't decide which to use, here are some different points that may be helpful in your decision.

Grammarly vs ProWritingAid

  • Grammarly is a writing enhancement tool that offers suggestions for grammar, vocabulary, and syntax whereas ProWritingAid offers world-class grammar and style checking, as well as advanced reports to help you strengthen your writing.
  • Grammarly provides Android and IOS apps whereas ProWritingAid doesn't have a mobile or IOS app.
  • Grammarly offers important suggestions about mistakes you've made whereas ProWritingAid  shows more suggestions than Grammarly but all recommendations are not accurate
  • Grammarly has a more friendly UI/UX whereas the ProWritingAid interface is not friendly as Grammarly.
  • Grammarly is an accurate grammar checker for non-fiction writing whereas ProWritingAid is an accurate grammar checker for fiction writers.
  • Grammarly finds grammar and punctuation mistakes, whereas ProWritingAid identifies run-on sentences and fragments.
  • Grammarly provides 24/7 support via submitting a ticket and sending emails. ProWritingAid’s support team is available via email, though the response time is approximately 48 hours.
  • Grammarly offers many features in its free plan, whereas ProWritingAid offers some basic features in the free plan.
  • Grammarly does not offer much feedback on big picture writing; ProWritingAid offers complete feedback on big picture writing.
  • Grammarly is a better option for accuracy, whereas ProWritingAid is better for handling fragmented sentences and dialogue. It can be quite useful for fiction writers.

ProWritingAid VS Grammarly: Pricing Difference

  • ProWritingAid comes with three pricing structures. The full-year cost of ProWritingAid is $79, while its lifetime plans cost $339. You also can opt for a monthly plan of $20.
  • Grammarly offers a Premium subscription for $30/month for a monthly plan  $20/month for quarterly and $12/month for an annual subscription.
  • The Business plan costs $12.50 per month for each member of your company.

ProWritingAid vs Grammarly – Pros and Cons

Grammarly Pros

  • It allows you to fix common mistakes like grammar and spelling.
  • Offers most features in the free plan
  • Allows you to edit a document without affecting the formatting.
  • Active and passive voice checker
  • Personal dictionary 
  • Plagiarism checker (paid version)
  • Proofread your writing and correct all punctuation, grammar, and spelling errors.
  • Allows you to make changes to a document without altering its formatting.
  • Helps users improve vocabulary
  • User-friendly interface
  • Browser extensions and MS word add-ons
  • Available on all major devices and platforms
  • Grammarly will also offer suggestions to improve your style.
  • Enhance the readability of your sentence
  • Free mobile apps 
  • Offers  free version

Grammarly Cons

  • Supports only English 
  • Customer support only via email
  • Limits to 150,000 words
  • Subscription plans can be a bit pricey 
  • Plagiarism checker is only available in a premium plan
  • Doesn’t offer a free trial
  • No refund policy
  • The free version is ideal for basic spelling and grammatical mistakes, but it does not correct advanced writing issues.
  • Some features are not available for Mac.

ProwritingAid Pros

  • It offers more than 20 different reports to help you improve your writing.
  • Less expensive than other grammar checkers.
  • This tool helps you strengthen your writing style as it offers big-picture feedback.
  • ProWritingAid has a life plan with no further payments required.
  • Compatible with Google Docs!
  • Prowritingaid works on both Windows and Mac.
  • They offer more integrations than most tools.

ProWritingAid Cons

  • Editing can be a little more time-consuming when you add larger passages of text.
  • ProWritingAid currently offers no mobile app for Android or iOS devices.
  • Plagiarism checker is only available in premium plans.
  • All recommendations are not accurate

Summarizing the Ginger VS Grammarly: My Recommendation

As both writing assistants are great in their own way, you need to choose the one that suits you best.

  • For example, go for Grammarly  if you are a non-fiction writer
  • Go for ProWritingAid if you are a fiction writer.
  • ProWritingAid is better at catching errors found in long-form content. However, Grammarly is more suited to short blog posts and other similar tasks.
  • ProWritingAid helps you clean up your writing by checking for style, structure, and content while Grammarly focuses on grammar and punctuation.
  • Grammarly has a more friendly UI/UX whereas; ProWritingAid offers complete feedback on big picture writing.

Both ProWritingAid and Grammarly are awesome writing tools, without a doubt. but as per my experience, Grammarly is a winner here because Grammarly helps you to review and edit your content. Grammarly highlights all the mistakes in your writing within seconds of copying and pasting the content into Grammarly’s editor or using the software’s native feature in other text editors.

Not only does it identify tiny grammatical and spelling errors, it tells you when you overlook punctuations where they are needed. And, beyond its plagiarism-checking capabilities, Grammarly helps you proofread your content. Even better, the software offers a free plan that gives you access to some of its features.

#9649. Detecting Chinese Characters in GBase 8a with REGEXP

To find rows containing Chinese characters in the China-domestically developed GBase 8a MPP database from GBASE, REGEXP is enough — provided the column uses the UTF8mb4 character set. This post shows two equivalent forms from the gbase client.

A test table tc with 7 rows mixing ASCII, digits and Chinese text:

The second form writes the CJK range [一-龥] (U+4E00–U+9FA5) directly into the SQL, which means the client connection's character set has to carry those bytes correctly. The first form avoids that entirely: unhex('5be4b8802de9bea55d') is the UTF8mb4 byte sequence of that same range — the opening bracket, the first character, the hyphen between the two Chinese characters, the last character and the closing bracket — expressed as hex, so no non-ASCII literal ever reaches the parser.

Looking ahead, the hex form is the safer default in a gbase cluster whenever SQL is passed through shells, scripts or drivers with uncertain encoding: it is pure ASCII, yet matches exactly the same range in the database. The trade-off is readability — keep a comment with the decoded range next to it, otherwise the next person to read the query has no idea what it matches.

What $30K grows to in 30 years at 7% annual return

The $30,000 average wedding figure you see everywhere is misleading. That number is skewed upward by luxury weddings in expensive metros like New York, San Francisco, and Los Angeles. The national median — the number where half of weddings cost more and half cost less — sits closer to $10,000 to $15,000. That distinction matters because it means a beautiful, memorable wedding is absolutely possible without spending five figures you do not have.

The FI perspective adds another layer: every dollar spent on a wedding is a dollar that cannot compound for decades. A $30,000 wedding invested for 30 years at a 7% average annual return grows to roughly $228,000. That does not mean you should elope in a courthouse (unless you want to), but it does mean you should spend intentionally on the categories that matter most to you and cut ruthlessly everywhere else.

Here is where the typical wedding dollar goes:

The biggest takeaway from this table: venue and catering are 60-70% of the total. If you can reduce those two categories, you change the entire math.

Not all wedding spending creates equal memories. Research consistently shows that couples remember three things most vividly years later: the ceremony itself, the food and drinks, and the photographs. Almost nobody remembers the chair covers, the napkin folds, or the custom monogram on the cocktail napkins.

That insight creates a clear FI-aligned strategy: splurge on what creates lasting memories (photographer, food, music) and minimize everything else.

The golden rule of wedding budgeting: if you cannot remember whether a detail was present at the last three weddings you attended, your guests will not notice either. Cut it without guilt.

The biggest financial mistake couples make is not setting a firm budget before visiting any vendors. Venues and vendors are skilled at upselling, and without a hard number in mind, costs spiral quickly. Start with a number you can pay in cash — wedding debt is one of the worst ways to begin a marriage and a direct threat to your FI timeline.

Follow this payment timeline to manage cash flow without credit card debt:

A practical savings strategy: divide your total budget by the number of months until the wedding and automate that transfer to a dedicated savings account. If your budget is $15,000 and your wedding is 15 months away, that is $1,000 per month. Treat it like any other savings goal on your FI path — automate, do not touch, and watch it grow.

For couples on the FI path, consider this reframe: every dollar you shave from the wedding budget is a dollar that starts compounding immediately. Cutting $5,000 from a $20,000 wedding and investing that savings at 7% for 25 years creates roughly $27,000 in future wealth. You can have a wonderful wedding and build wealth simultaneously — but only if you plan intentionally from the start.

Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

Before finalizing your wedding budget, run the compound interest math on any amount you are considering spending. A $30,000 wedding invested at 7% for 30 years becomes roughly $228,000. A $15,000 wedding invested at 7% for 30 years becomes roughly $114,000. This is not an argument against celebrating — it is an argument for spending intentionally on what matters to you and cutting everything else. The couple who spends $15,000 on a joyful celebration and invests the other $15,000 gets both the wedding and a significant head start on financial independence.

#9647. Architecting Production-Ready n8n AI Workflows: Queue Mode and Security

Chaining together an AI agent or webhook automation in n8n takes five minutes in a local environment. But running those workflows under real production workloads is an entirely different engineering challenge.

The moment inbound webhook traffic spikes, your single-node instance starts dropping connections. If an upstream LLM API throws a 429 rate limit or invalid JSON response, fragile chains halt mid-execution. Worse, exposing unauthenticated webhook endpoints leaves internal pipelines open to replay attacks and unauthorized payloads.

To move self-hosted n8n automations into production, you need architectural patterns designed for resilience: decoupled worker queues, cryptographically verified webhooks, and structured fallback routing.

Here are three foundational patterns you can implement directly in your infrastructure.

By default, n8n runs executions in the same process that handles webhooks and serves the UI. Under heavy load, memory leaks or intensive code executions can crash the entire system.

To scale horizontally, decouple your webhook receivers and background task runners using Redis queue mode:

This setup allows the main n8n instance to focus solely on receiving webhooks and scheduling, offloading compute-heavy tasks to one or more independent worker containers.

Never process incoming webhook payloads from external services (like Stripe or GitHub) without verifying their signature. Running an unverified payload through an LLM agent creates prompt injection vectors and consumes token budgets unnecessarily.

Place an n8n Code Node directly after your Webhook trigger to compute and verify the HMAC signature:

If the signature doesn't match, execution halts before downstream LLM nodes or database writes can be triggered.

Production AI pipelines must handle rate limits and transient provider outages cleanly. Instead of routing all tasks to expensive frontier models, configure a conditional routing router that tries lower-latency models first and falls back gracefully:

If you want to skip building queue architectures, verification snippets, and agentic error handling from scratch, check out The n8n AI Automation Architecture Vault.

Grab the templates, import them directly into your self-hosted n8n instance, and start shipping enterprise-grade automations today.

#9646. SQL Server Licensing in 2026: When Standard Is Enough (and When Enterprise Pays Off)

Same 16-core server, same SQL Server 2025. One license bill is $31,560, the other is $120,984. That's the gap between Standard and Enterprise, and in my experience most teams paying for Enterprise use only one or two of the features that justify it.

Here's how to work out which one you actually need.

US Open no-level list prices from Microsoft (November 2026). Your real price depends on your agreement and reseller.

Express and both Developer editions are free. Developer is for dev and test only, never production.

Standard can also be licensed as $989 per server + $230 per user or device (CAL). On a 16-core box the math breaks even at roughly 133 users:

If you have a small, known set of users on a big server, CALs can save a lot. If the database sits behind a public web app, you can't count users, so it's per-core.

Standard got a real upgrade: it now supports up to 32 cores and 256 GB of memory. Express goes up to 50 GB per database. A lot of workloads that "needed Enterprise for the RAM" no longer do.

If none of those are hurting you today, Standard is very likely enough. (On the index point: most nightly rebuild jobs aren't needed anyway. I covered that here.)

With SA you get free passive replicas for HA and DR: you don't pay for a secondary that only waits for a failover. Teams that license the standby server fully are paying twice.

For the full Azure-vs-VM cost picture, see my real cost comparison.

Prices are Microsoft list prices from November 2026. Licensing terms are detailed and change often. Confirm your case with Microsoft or a licensing partner before buying. This is general information, not licensing advice.

#9645. What is Blockchain: Everything You Need to Know (2022)


If you want to pay online, you need to register an account and provide credit card information. If you don't have a credit card, you can pay with bank transfer. With the rise of cryptocurrencies, these methods may become old.

Imagine a world in which you can do transactions and many other things without having to give your personal information. A world in which you don’t need to rely on banks or governments anymore. Sounds amazing, right? That’s exactly what blockchain technology allows us to do.

It’s like your computer’s hard drive. blockchain is a technology that lets you store data in digital blocks, which are connected together like links in a chain. 

Blockchain technology was originally invented in 1991 by two mathematicians, Stuart Haber and W. Scot Stornetta. They first proposed the system to ensure that timestamps could not be tampered with.

A few years later, in 1998, software developer Nick Szabo proposed using a similar kind of technology to secure a digital payments system he called “Bit Gold.” However, this innovation was not adopted until Satoshi Nakamoto claimed to have invented the first Blockchain and Bitcoin.

So, What is Blockchain?

A blockchain is a distributed database shared between the nodes of a computer network. It saves information in digital format. Many people first heard of blockchain technology when they started to look up information about bitcoin.

Blockchain is used in cryptocurrency systems to ensure secure, decentralized records of transactions.

Blockchain allowed people to guarantee the fidelity and security of a record of data without the need for a third party to ensure accuracy.

To understand how a blockchain works, Consider these basic steps:

  • Blockchain collects information in “blocks”.
  • A block has a storage capacity, and once it's used up, it can be closed and linked to a previously served block.
  • Blocks form chains, which are called “Blockchains.”
  • More information will be added to the block with the most content until its capacity is full. The process repeats itself.
  • Each block in the chain has an exact timestamp and can't be changed.

Let’s get to know more about the blockchain.

How does blockchain work?

Blockchain records digital information and distributes it across the network without changing it. The information is distributed among many users and stored in an immutable, permanent ledger that can't be changed or destroyed. That's why blockchain is also called "Distributed Ledger Technology" or DLT.

Here’s how it works:

  • Someone or a computer will transacts
  • The transaction is transmitted throughout the network.
  • A network of computers can confirm the transaction.
  • When it is confirmed a transaction is added to a block
  • The blocks are linked together to create a history.

And that’s the beauty of it! The process may seem complicated, but it’s done in minutes with modern technology. And because technology is advancing rapidly, I expect things to move even more quickly than ever.

  • A new transaction is added to the system. It is then relayed to a network of computers located around the world. The computers then solve equations to ensure the authenticity of the transaction.
  • Once a transaction is confirmed, it is placed in a block after the confirmation. All of the blocks are chained together to create a permanent history of every transaction.

How are Blockchains used?

Even though blockchain is integral to cryptocurrency, it has other applications. For example, blockchain can be used for storing reliable data about transactions. Many people confuse blockchain with cryptocurrencies like bitcoin and ethereum.

Blockchain already being adopted by some big-name companies, such as Walmart, AIG, Siemens, Pfizer, and Unilever. For example, IBM's Food Trust uses blockchain to track food's journey before reaching its final destination.

Although some of you may consider this practice excessive, food suppliers and manufacturers adhere to the policy of tracing their products because bacteria such as E. coli and Salmonella have been found in packaged foods. In addition, there have been isolated cases where dangerous allergens such as peanuts have accidentally been introduced into certain products.

Tracing and identifying the sources of an outbreak is a challenging task that can take months or years. Thanks to the Blockchain, however, companies now know exactly where their food has been—so they can trace its location and prevent future outbreaks.

Blockchain technology allows systems to react much faster in the event of a hazard. It also has many other uses in the modern world.

What is Blockchain Decentralization?

Blockchain technology is safe, even if it’s public. People can access the technology using an internet connection.

Have you ever been in a situation where you had all your data stored at one place and that one secure place got compromised? Wouldn't it be great if there was a way to prevent your data from leaking out even when the security of your storage systems is compromised?

Blockchain technology provides a way of avoiding this situation by using multiple computers at different locations to store information about transactions. If one computer experiences problems with a transaction, it will not affect the other nodes.

Instead, other nodes will use the correct information to cross-reference your incorrect node. This is called “Decentralization,” meaning all the information is stored in multiple places.

Blockchain guarantees your data's authenticity—not just its accuracy, but also its irreversibility. It can also be used to store data that are difficult to register, like legal contracts, state identifications, or a company's product inventory.

Pros and Cons of Blockchain

Blockchain has many advantages and disadvantages. 

Pros

  • Accuracy is increased because there is no human involvement in the verification process.
  • One of the great things about decentralization is that it makes information harder to tamper with.
  • Safe, private, and easy transactions
  • Provides a banking alternative and safe storage of personal information

Cons

  • Data storage has limits.
  • The regulations are always changing, as they differ from place to place.
  • It has a risk of being used for illicit activities 

Frequently Asked Questions About Blockchain

I’ll answer the most frequently asked questions about blockchain in this section.

Is Blockchain a cryptocurrency?

Blockchain is not a cryptocurrency but a technology that makes cryptocurrencies possible. It's a digital ledger that records every transaction seamlessly.

Is it possible for Blockchain to be hacked?

Yes, blockchain can be theoretically hacked, but it is a complicated task to be achieved. A network of users constantly reviews it, which makes hacking the blockchain difficult.

What is the most prominent blockchain company?

Coinbase Global is currently the biggest blockchain company in the world. The company runs a commendable infrastructure, services, and technology for the digital currency economy.

Who owns Blockchain?

Blockchain is a decentralized technology. It’s a chain of distributed ledgers connected with nodes. Each node can be any electronic device. Thus, one owns blockhain.

What is the difference between Bitcoin and Blockchain technology?

Bitcoin is a cryptocurrency, which is powered by Blockchain technology while Blockchain is a distributed ledger of cryptocurrency 

What is the difference between Blockchain and a Database?

Generally a database is a collection of data which can be stored and organized using a database management system. The people who have access to the database can view or edit the information stored there. The client-server network architecture is used to implement databases. whereas a blockchain is a growing list of records, called blocks, stored in a distributed system. Each block contains a cryptographic hash of the previous block, timestamp and transaction information. Modification of data is not allowed due to the design of the blockchain. The technology allows decentralized control and eliminates risks of data modification by other parties.

Final Saying

Blockchain has a wide spectrum of applications and, over the next 5-10 years, we will likely see it being integrated into all sorts of industries. From finance to healthcare, blockchain could revolutionize the way we store and share data. Although there is some hesitation to adopt blockchain systems right now, that won't be the case in 2022-2023 (and even less so in 2026). Once people become more comfortable with the technology and understand how it can work for them, owners, CEOs and entrepreneurs alike will be quick to leverage blockchain technology for their own gain. Victoria, Seychelles, November 27th, 2026/Chainwire/--The BASIS Card returns money differently. Announced today by BASIS DIGITAL INFRASTRUCTURE LTD, the payment card credits cashback in the asset used for each eligible purchase, with Platinum cardholders qualifying for 10% cashback during the introductory Launch Boost period.

For digital asset holders, the principle is straightforward. Spend Bitcoin and receive Bitcoin back. Pay with Ethereum and receive Ethereum back. There are no reward points to redeem or proprietary platform tokens to manage. Cashback is credited in an asset the cardholder already uses, giving everyday spending a direct connection to their digital asset holdings.

The opening of first-round applications marks an expansion of BASIS's existing digital asset infrastructure into everyday payments. Applications are submitted at https://basis.pro/card and close on December 31, 2026, at 23:59 UTC.

The BASIS Card is available in Standard, finished in matte black composite, and Platinum, produced in metal. Applicants select their preferred edition when submitting their waitlist application, with qualification determined by their active staking position.

Each edition has a separate staking eligibility threshold, as detailed below. BASIS measures the value of the applicant's active staking position against the requirement for their selected tier. The position is assessed at submission and re-checked at the close of the application period.

Participants can therefore review the benefits of each edition alongside its staking requirements before deciding which card to apply for. Final issuance remains subject to the issuing partner's independent review.

Both editions feature an introductory Launch Boost period, beginning on the date of card issuance. During this period, cardholders receive enhanced cashback rates, higher monthly reward caps, and additional subscription benefits.

*All monetary figures are expressed in USD. Physical card issuance fees include applicable shipping charges.

Launch Boost runs for three months following issuance, after which each card returns to its respective base benefits. Standard and Platinum also feature rate-lock periods of 12 and 24 months, respectively, subject to the applicable program terms.

Along with cashback, the card program brings together subscription rebates of 50% or 100%, depending on the edition and benefit period, across a catalog of over 80 subscriptions. Travel and additional card benefits include two annual airport lounge visits, a 3 GB eSIM, and one additional card, subject to tier eligibility and applicable terms. Standard cardholders benefit from a 2% FX fee, while Platinum cardholders pay no FX fee during Launch Boost. Both editions provide immediate access to a virtual card upon activation, with Platinum participants also receiving priority and dedicated support.

The defining feature of the BASIS Card is what happens after a purchase. Where conventional reward programs may require cardholders to accumulate points or convert rewards into their preferred currency, BASIS keeps the cashback denomination consistent with the asset spent.

Cashback on eligible settled purchases is credited directly to the cardholder's Funding Wallet. A purchase made using BTC returns BTC, leaving the recipient free to decide how to use the reward.

Cardholders who wish to stake their cashback can do so separately under the platform's ordinary conversion rules. Cashback does not automatically enter an existing staking position, and card rewards remain independent of staking yield.

Submitting a card application also leaves existing staking positions, lock-up periods, Dynamic Reward Rates, boosters, and stToken balances unchanged.

Applications are free and limited to one per account during Round 01. Participants must hold at least USD 1,000 in eligible BASIS wallet value at submission, maintain an account in good standing, and satisfy the staking requirements for their selected card edition.

Once BASIS approves a waitlist application, the applicant receives further instructions and a secure Know Your Customer (KYC) verification link. The issuing partner then conducts its own review, covering identity verification, residency, regional eligibility, sanctions screening, and supporting documentation.

Waitlist approval permits applicants to proceed to the next stage and does not constitute final card approval, activation, or issuance.

Further information on card eligibility, benefits, fees, and application requirements is available in the official BASIS Card Program documentation.

#9643. Most Frequently Asked Questions About Affiliate Marketing

Affiliate marketing is a way to make money by promoting the products and services of other people and companies. You don't need to create your product or service, just promote existing ones. That's why it's so easy to get started with affiliate marketing. You can even get started with no budget at all!

An affiliate program is a package of information you create for your product, which is then made available to potential publishers. The program will typically include details about the product and its retail value, commission levels, and promotional materials. Many affiliate programs are managed via an affiliate network like ShareASale, which acts as a platform to connect publishers and advertisers, but it is also possible to offer your program directly.

Affiliate networks connect publishers to advertisers.  Affiliate networks make money by charging fees to the merchants who advertise with them; these merchants are known as advertisers. The percentage of each sale that the advertiser pays is negotiated between the merchant and the affiliate network.

Dropshipping is a method of selling that allows you to run an online store without having to stock products. You advertise the products as if you owned them, but when someone makes an order, you create a duplicate order with the distributor at a reduced price. The distributor takes care of the post and packaging on your behalf. As affiliate marketing is based on referrals and this type of drop shipping requires no investment in inventory when a customer buys through the affiliate link, no money exchanges hands.

Performance marketing is a method of marketing that pays for performance, like when a sale is made or an ad is clicked This can include methods like PPC (pay-per-click) or display advertising. Affiliate marketing is one form of performance marketing where commissions are paid out to affiliates on a performance basis when they click on their affiliate link and make a purchase or action.

Smartphones are essentially miniature computers, so publishers can display the same websites and offers that are available on a PC. But mobiles also offer specific tools not available on computers, and these can be used to good effect for publishers. Publishers can optimize their ads for mobile users by making them easy to access by this audience. Publishers can also make good use of text and instant messaging to promote their offers. As the mobile market is predicted to make up 80% of traffic in the future, publishers who do not promote on mobile devices are missing out on a big opportunity.

The best way to find affiliate publishers is on reputable networks like ShareASale Cj(Commission Junction), Awin, and Impact radius. These networks have a strict application process and compliance checks, which means that all affiliates are trustworthy.

An affiliate disclosure statement discloses to the reader that there may be affiliate links on a website, for which a commission may be paid to the publisher if visitors follow these links and make purchases.

Publishers promote their programs through a variety of means, including blogs, websites, email marketing, and pay-per-click ads. Social media has a huge interactive audience, making this platform a good source of potential traffic.

A super affiliate is an affiliate partner who consistently drives a large majority of sales from any program they promote, compared to other affiliate partners involved in that program.  Affiliates make a lot of money from affiliate marketing Pat Flynn earned more than $50000 in 2013 from affiliate marketing.

Because the Internet is so widespread, affiliate programs can be promoted in any country. Affiliate strategies that are set internationally need to be tailored to the language of the targeted country.

Affiliate marketing can help you grow your business in the following ways:

One of the best ways to work with qualified affiliates is to hire an affiliate marketing agency that works with all the networks. Affiliates are carefully selected and go through a rigorous application process to be included in the network.

Affiliate marketing is generally associated with websites, but there are other ways to promote your affiliate links, including:

To build your affiliate marketing business, you don't have to invest money in the beginning. You can sign up for free with any affiliate network and start promoting their brands right away.

Commission rates are typically based on a percentage of the total sale and in some cases can also be a flat fee for each transaction. The rates are set by the merchant.

Some merchants run their affiliate programs internally, while others choose to contract out management to a network or an external agency.

Copilot is a suite of tools that help eCommerce businesses maintain real-time communication with customers around the clock at every stage of the funnel. Promote products, recover shopping carts and send updates or reminders directly through Messenger.

The AI-powered moderation tool automatically assigns a score to each review and flags reviews with negative sentiment so you can focus on quality control instead of manually reviewing every post.

Albert identifies potential customers that match those traits, and runs trial campaigns on a small group of customers—with results refined by Albert himself—before launching it on a larger scale.

Albert plugs into your existing marketing technology stack, so you still have access to your accounts, ads, search, social media, and more. Albert maps tracking and attribution to your source of truth so you can determine which channels are driving your business.

There are many tools and companies out there that offer AI tools, but this is a small list of resources that we have found to be helpful. As marketing evolves at such a rapid pace, new marketing strategies will be invented that we haven't even dreamed of yet. #9641. What is high-extraction flour, exactly?  : A baker’s guide to our new T85 Baker's Reserve Bread Flour.

High-extraction flour is a technical term that often prompts a lot of confusion from those unfamiliar with it. But with the debut of our new high-extraction flour, known as Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour, we’re breaking down just what it is and why it's a great choice for avid bread makers.

The extraction rate of a flour refers to how much of the original grain — the bran, germ, and endosperm — ends up in the final flour. A high-extraction flour typically has an extraction rate of about 80% to 90%, meaning some of the bran and germ have been sifted out, but it still retains much of the original grain. Our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour is a T85 flour, meaning its extraction rate is 85%.

To put that in perspective, whole wheat flour has an extraction rate of 100%; it retains the entirety of the grain, including the bran, germ, and endosperm.

High-extraction flour falls between white and whole wheat flour. It’s lighter and less coarse than whole wheat flour because some of the bran has been sifted out, but it still retains more flavor, nutrients, and color than white flour, since it retains much of the original grain.

High-extraction flour is popular for artisan bread baking because it offers a balance of nutrition and good gluten development. It’s great for rustic loaves, baguettes, and pizza dough, and particularly well-suited for sourdough baking because it strikes a balance between flavor, nutrition, fermentation, and dough strength.

You can substitute our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour 1:1 for bread flour (by weight or volume) in artisanal bread recipes; it can also be used 1:1 to replace the total flour in recipes that call for a combination of all-purpose and whole wheat flour. If you're subbing Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour for all-purpose flour in a bread recipe, you may find you need to add slightly more liquid to the recipe.

Bread bakers love high-extraction flour for artisan bread and sourdough because it offers the flavor and nutrition of whole grain flour; the stronger gluten development and more open crumb you get from white flour; and better fermentation from the minerals present in the bran and germ, which feed the wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria in sourdough starter, promoting more active fermentation.

If you want a loaf of bread that’s more flavorful and nutritious than bread made with exclusively white flour, but that still rises high and has an open crumb, high-extraction flour is a great choice.

Yes — in fact, it’s a great choice for feeding starter because of the sourdough-friendly minerals present in the flour, which boost activity in your starter.

Yes! T85 is a French specification that refers to the extraction rate (85%) of the flour. Our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour is a T85 flour, meaning the extraction rate is 85%. If you have a recipe that calls for T85, this flour is the perfect choice.

Find our high-extraction Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour online.

#9631. We Tried 6 Store-Bought Pumpkin Pies—These Are The Only 2 Worth Serving At Thanksgiving

A handful of things are non-negotiable at Thanksgiving. You need turkey, stuffing, cranberry sauce, and, of course, a slice of pie to round out your meal. And pumpkin pie is the undeniable star of the dessert table.

But sometimes you're strapped for time and have too much on your plate (pun intended) to whip something up from scratch. So we tried six different grocery store pumpkin pies to find the best store-bought shortcut. And our team's verdict was pretty unanimous, even if it’s a bit hard to hear: No premade pie will ever taste as good as a homemade one.

It primarily comes down to the crust. Frozen and pre-baked pies typically rely on vegetable-based fat instead of butter because they’re more affordable, reliable, and shelf-stable—but that comes at a cost. You not only miss out on the decadent, buttery taste, but the crusts can also leave an unpleasant film on your tongue.

That said, when you need to outsource to the grocery store, we found two options that will work in a pinch.

The pie that we’d feel most confident bringing to Thanksgiving dinner comes straight from the Whole Foods bakery department. That’s not to say it’s perfect, though. The crust is almost upsettingly pale, but it’s made with real butter and only a little bit of palm oil. And since it doesn’t leave a noticeable film and still lets the butter flavor shine, we’ll let this one slide.

Once you look past the crust’s color, this pie is solid overall. The filling is decadent, not too sweet, and creamy without being mushy. Whole Foods doesn’t shy away from the spices, either.

Senior Editor Samantha MacAvoy noted that the warming spices are nicely balanced, while Designer Alison Dominguez said, “The flavor was exactly how a pumpkin pie should taste.”

Costco’s pumpkin pie isn’t perfect: The crust uses palm oil-based shortening rather than butter and can develop a soggy bottom if you buy it too far in advance. (And it doesn’t hold a candle to the warehouse’s holy grail pumpkin cheesecake.) But it has a cult following for a reason, and not just because of its $5.99 price tag.

Even with its faults, the crust has great flavor and enough salt to create a balanced bite. Dominguez appreciated how it was “flaky and not too thick, and most importantly, it let the pie filling itself shine.” News and Features Editor Amanda Mactas chose Costco’s pie as her number one pick. “It all seemed to melt together in one creamy bite,” she said.

And at over three pounds, this dessert is the indisputable champion if you want to feed a crowd for less.

What's your FI number? Calculate it in 60 seconds

Before comparing your balance to anyone else's, you need to know what the benchmarks actually include. Most retirement savings data from Vanguard, Fidelity, and the Federal Reserve covers:

What these numbers typically exclude: taxable brokerage accounts, real estate equity, HSA balances invested for retirement, pension values, and Social Security. For FI-minded savers, this distinction matters enormously — your total investable net worth is almost certainly larger than your "retirement savings" as defined by these surveys.

The gap between average and median retirement savings is one of the most important distinctions in personal finance. The average gets pulled upward by high-balance accounts — a single person with $5 million in their 401(k) dramatically inflates the average for their age group. The median (the middle number when all balances are ranked) gives you a far more honest picture of what a typical American actually has saved.

Notice how the gap widens with age. By 65+, the average is 3.3 times the median — meaning a small number of disciplined savers (or high earners) are pulling the average far above what most people actually have. The median tells you what a typical person in each age group actually holds. If you are above the median, you are doing better than half of Americans your age. But "better than average" and "on track for a secure retirement" are very different standards.

Vanguard's annual "How America Saves" report and Fidelity's quarterly retirement analysis provide the most comprehensive snapshots of what Americans hold in their workplace retirement accounts. These numbers reflect defined-contribution plan balances only — primarily 401(k) and 403(b) accounts.

Average balance: $13,265. Median balance: $5,400. Most savers in this bracket have been contributing for fewer than five years. The biggest advantage this group has is time — a 25-year-old contributing $6,000 per year with a 7% average return will accumulate over $1.2 million by age 65 without ever increasing their contribution. The FI community emphasizes that getting started early matters far more than starting with large contributions.

Average balance: $53,300. Median balance: $21,000. This is where employer matches start compounding meaningfully. Fidelity data shows that employees who have been contributing consistently since their 20s have balances 2.5 to 3 times higher than those who started in their 30s. The typical employer match adds 3-6% of salary — effectively free money that many employees still leave on the table. According to Vanguard, roughly 25% of eligible employees do not contribute enough to capture their full employer match.

Average balance: $142,069. Median balance: $60,763. Earnings typically peak in this decade, making it the critical window for aggressive savings. FIRE-path savers in this age bracket commonly have $500,000 to $1 million or more saved by maximizing their 401(k) ($25,500 in 2027), HSA ($4,500 individual / $9,000 family), and Roth IRA ($7,000) — then directing additional savings into taxable brokerage accounts.

Fidelity's guideline of 1x salary by 30 and 10x salary by 67 is a reasonable starting point for traditional retirement planning. But for FI seekers, these benchmarks are the floor, not the ceiling. The ChooseFI community consistently demonstrates that saving 40-60% of income — rather than the national average of 4.6% — compresses the timeline from 40 working years down to 10-17.

If your balance is below the median for your age group, you are not alone — and you are not stuck. The math of compound growth means that aggressive action in your 40s and 50s can still produce a secure retirement or even an early one.

The IRS provides additional contribution room for savers age 50 and older. In 2027, the 401(k) catch-up contribution is $7,500 on top of the standard $25,500 limit, for a total of $31,000. IRA catch-up contributions add $1,000 to the standard $7,000 limit. HSA catch-up for those 55+ adds another $1,000. Combined with employer matching, a 50-year-old couple can potentially shelter $80,000 or more per year in tax-advantaged accounts.

Most financial advice focuses on investment returns, but the variable you control most directly is your savings rate. Moving from a 10% savings rate to a 30% savings rate has a dramatically larger impact on your retirement timeline than chasing an extra 2% of investment return. A household earning $120,000 that increases from 10% to 30% savings — a shift of $24,000 per year — adds roughly $600,000 to their retirement balance over 15 years (assuming 7% average returns).

The FI community's core insight is that savings rate is the primary driver of financial independence. At a 50% savings rate, you can reach FI in roughly 17 years regardless of income level. At 60%, it compresses to about 12 years. At 70%, you are looking at under 10 years. These numbers are independent of salary — they depend only on the ratio of savings to spending.

The average American contributes 4.6% of salary to their 401(k), receives a 3-4% employer match, and saves little outside of that. FIRE-path savers typically max every available tax-advantaged account, maintain savings rates of 40-60%, invest in low-cost index funds, and direct overflow savings into taxable brokerage accounts. The result: FIRE savers in their 40s commonly have $500,000 to $1.5 million in total investable assets — 5 to 10 times the national median for their age group. The difference is not income; many FIRE success stories come from median-income households that simply saved aggressively and avoided lifestyle inflation.

If you are 40 with $50,000 saved and feeling behind, shifting from a 10% savings rate to a 40% savings rate on a $100,000 income adds $30,000 per year to your investment accounts. At 7% average returns, that alone grows to over $950,000 in 15 years — before counting the $50,000 you already have. Starting late is not ideal, but a high savings rate compresses the timeline dramatically.

Most employers allow you to change your 401(k) contribution rate at any time. Increasing by 2% of salary is small enough that you will barely notice the paycheck reduction, but it compounds dramatically over time. Repeat this increase every six months until you are maxing out your 401(k).

Roughly one in four employees leaves free employer match money on the table. If your employer matches 50% of contributions up to 6% of salary, you need to contribute at least 6% to capture the full match. This is an instant 50% return on your money — no investment can beat it.

A Roth IRA provides tax-free growth and tax-free withdrawals in retirement, with no required minimum distributions. The 2026 limit is $7,000 ($8,000 if 50+). If your income exceeds the Roth limits, use the backdoor Roth conversion strategy to contribute indirectly.

The average is pulled upward by a small percentage of very high-balance accounts. If nine people have $10,000 saved and one person has $1,000,000, the average is $109,000 but the median is $10,000. The median gives a far more accurate picture of what a typical American has saved. Always compare yourself to the median, not the average.

Yes — employer matching contributions are part of your retirement savings balance. In a typical arrangement, an employer matches 50% of your contributions up to 6% of salary. Retirement planning should focus on investable assets — accounts you can convert to income without selling your primary residence.

A common guideline is 10-12x your pre-retirement income. For a household earning $100,000, that means $1,000,000 to $1,200,000 in retirement savings. The 4% rule suggests you can withdraw 4% of your portfolio annually with a high probability of not running out over 30 years — so $1 million supports roughly $40,000 per year in withdrawals.

It is never too late, but the urgency increases with age. A 40-year-old saving $20,000 per year at 7% returns will accumulate roughly $1 million by age 65. A 50-year-old has access to catch-up contributions ($7,500 extra in a 401(k)) and can still build $400,000 to $600,000 in 15 years with aggressive saving. The key is maximizing savings rate immediately rather than trying to make up ground through risky investments.

The average retirement savings benchmarks are useful directional guides, but they should not define your target. Most Americans are dramatically undersaved — the median 401(k) balance at retirement age is under $75,000, which supports only about $2,860 per year in withdrawals using the 4% rule. That is not a retirement plan; it is a supplement to Social Security at best. The FI community takes a fundamentally different approach: define your actual annual spending, multiply by 25, and work backward to a savings rate that gets you there. Whether your number is $750,000 or $3 million, the path is the same — maximize tax-advantaged accounts, invest in low-cost index funds, maintain a high savings rate, and let compound growth do the heavy lifting. If you are behind the benchmarks, the single most impactful action is increasing your savings rate, not chasing higher returns.

#9619. Ciara Has One Holiday Cooking Rule & You Really Don't Want To Break It

She's all for getting creative with Oreos, although she has much stronger feelings about the rest of the menu.

Ciara has one request for whoever’s in charge of Christmas dinner: Please, whatever you do, make sure you’re up for the assignment. She’s willing to embrace a little holiday mess, but apparently, there’s a limit to how far that generosity extends into the kitchen.

“All I know is you better not burn no turkey. That’s a culinary crime,” the Grammy-winning singer told Delish. And if you're cooking without a backup bird? You might want to pay especially close attention to that oven. “You better get it right on the first try.”

Ciara, a mom of four, certainly understands how quickly the festivities can get away from you. “Christmas in our house is full of love, excitement and a little chaos,” she said in a statement. But when it comes to the actual Christmas menu, she’s got some traditions she’s pretty attached to, many of which go all the way back to her childhood in Atlanta, Georgia.

"If you know one thing about us ATLians, you have Thanksgiving on Christmas. The same meal comes back around again," she told Delish.

And we’re talking a serious Southern spread: turkey legs, mac and cheese, candied yams, collard greens, chitlins, and pig feet. She's no longer making pig feet these days, but the other familiar favorites have stuck around. Ciara says those dishes still “make me very happy,” which is as good a reason as any to keep a family tradition going.

Personally, I think we’ve been limiting Thanksgiving dinner to one holiday for far too long.

#9604. The 7 Most Common Mistakes Home Cooks Make When Cooking Mashed Potatoes

The simplest Thanksgiving side deserves better.

In a traditional Thanksgiving meal, mashed potatoes are a seemingly simple side dish that does a lot of heavy lifting. They're the perfect vessel for a puddle of gravy, and they’re a creamy complement to everything else on your plate—yes, even your aunt's questionable green bean casserole.

Mashed potatoes prove you can transform even the humblest ingredients into something magical. And yet, we've all somehow still eaten bad ones. With a recipe this basic, even the smallest mistakes have nowhere to hide.

Thankfully, those mistakes are 100% avoidable. We rounded up the most common ways to mess up mashed potatoes so that yours turn out as delicious as possible this holiday season.

It doesn’t matter if you cut your potatoes into a fine dice or rough chunks. Whatever size you pick, stick with it. Making sure your potato pieces are roughly the same size will help them all cook at the same rate. If your knife work is haphazard, you may end up with some pieces that are perfectly cooked, others that are waterlogged and mushy, and some that are still firm in the center.

Like pasta, potatoes need a good amount of seasoning to really shine—which is why salting the cooking water is so important. You can be generous with the salt, since much of it stays in the water and ends up going down the drain. When you start seasoning early in the cooking process, it’s easier to build flavor and adjust as you go.

In the hustle of cooking all of your Thanksgiving dishes, you may be tempted to boil your potatoes ahead of time and mash them later in the day. But it’s always better to work with potatoes while they’re still hot and easier to mash. Waiting until they’re cool will likely require far more elbow grease—and you’ll still end up with uneven chunks.

A smooth, creamy mash is the height of decadence. To make sure the potatoes are lump-free, some people may reach for a blender—but this is one of the most consequential mistakes you can make. Potatoes are naturally starchy, and the more you work them, the more starch gets released from their cell walls. Breaking out the blender may be well-intentioned, but it can leave you with potatoes that are gummy and gluey. Instead, opt for the right tool, like a hand masher, food mill, or potato ricer.

Another important thing to consider is that potato starches continue absorbing moisture as mashed potatoes sit. They can soak up the milk you’ve added, leaving your potatoes dry and dense. Don’t be afraid to add more liquid—or at least keep some extra on hand to loosen up your mash before serving.

Anthony Bourdain famously pointed to generous amounts of salt and butter as part of what makes restaurant food taste so good. That’s especially true for mashed potatoes. You may be scared to add more than a light sprinkle of salt, but don’t forget to taste and adjust the seasoning before serving. A little extra salt can make all the difference for your Thanksgiving dinner.

Whether you’re feeding your immediate family or a small army, you should always make a big batch of mashed potatoes. This side is one of the most popular components of a Thanksgiving menu, so it never hurts to make extra. It’s also one of the most versatile dishes for repurposing leftovers. You can transform them into gnocchi, shepherd’s pie, or crispy fried croquettes. It may require more mashing in the moment, but your future self will thank you.
